title: Near addressing folds in upstream llvm-mos leave dangling DBG_VALUEs
summary: On upstream llvm-mos 06bc967d2668, a -g near access whose address the MOS legalizer folds into an addressing mode fails -verify-machineinstrs with "Generic virtual register use cannot be undef": a pointer plus a zero-extended byte index (absolute indexed or indirect indexed) at O0 and O2 on mos6502 and mosw65816, and a near global plus a constant at O0. Mechanism: MOSLegalizerInfo::selectAddressingMode (tryAbsoluteAddressing, tryAbsoluteIndexedAddressing, indirect indexed) replaces the access, the G_PTR_ADD that computed its pointer is left with only a debug use, the legalizer erases it, and the generic salvageDebugInfoForDbgValue (llvm/lib/CodeGen/CodeGenCommonISel.cpp) skips a DBG_VALUE it cannot salvage instead of dropping its location, so the DBG_VALUE names an erased register. It is not fixed here. Classification: the trigger is MOS-specific (the MOS legalizer performs addressing-mode folds that erase address arithmetic; other GlobalISel targets fold addresses during selection), and the missing fallback is in generic GlobalISel code. Proposed upstream fix: in llvm-mos, make salvageDebugInfoForDbgValue set an unsalvageable DBG_VALUE to $noreg (setDebugValueUndef), as the IR salvage does, and salvage a G_PTR_ADD with a constant offset as DW_OP_plus_uconst; that generic change also repairs the far sites. A MOS-local alternative is a helper after each fold, like the far-series dropDeadFarAddressDebugUses.

prior_work.source_assessment: Upstream 06bc967d2668 salvageDebugInfoForDbgValue continues past a DBG_VALUE when computeSalvageReplacements returns nothing, which covers every G_PTR_ADD; the MOS near fold helpers do not drop the debug users of addresses they make dead.
prior_work.binary_assessment: The upstream-base llc p-321-00 (assertions) exits 134 with the signature for nidx.ll (mos6502 O0/O2, mosw65816 O2), ngidx.ll and nearfield.ll (O2) and ngfield.ll (O0).
prior_work.decision: The far records cover address-space-2 fold sites in the far series and are repaired there by a far-only helper; these near sites exist in upstream llvm-mos without any far code, so they are a separate canonical record for an upstream report. No upstream issue or PR reports them (search of 2026-10-01).
